currentContext.business: Jubilant FoodWorks Limited (JFL), incorporated in 1995, is an emerging-markets food-service company whose Group network comprises 3,636 stores across India, Turkey, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Azerbaijan and Georgia. It holds franchise rights for three global brands - Domino's, Popeyes and Dunkin' - and operates two own-brands, Hong's Kitchen (an Indo-Chinese QSR brand in India) and COFFY (a cafe brand in Turkey). The Company serves over 50 million customers annually across more than 650 cities through an integrated ecosystem of stores, supply chain infrastructure, technology platforms and last-mile delivery operations.

currentContext.strengths: Brand Leadership and Innovation: Domino's Pizza is described as one of India's most iconic and dominant food-service brands with significant market share in the organised pizza category, built over three decades of local menu innovation, value positioning and fast delivery.|Multi-brand portfolio spanning pizza (Domino's), fried chicken (Popeyes) and Indo-Chinese (Hong's Kitchen) targeting diverse consumer occasions and price points, capturing a larger share of wallet.|Scaled Digital Ecosystem: proprietary AI platforms - Location.AI (site selection/catchment optimisation), Restaurant.AI (computer-vision store monitoring, dynamic delivery-zone/discount management) and Delivery.AI (rider onboarding under 30 minutes, order allocation) - are described as strengthening the Company's competitive moat.|Common operating platform (supply chain, technology, store operations, analytics, talent) that allows JFL to scale multiple brands and geographies more efficiently and improve capital efficiency.|Scale as the world's largest Domino's franchisee by store count, with 3,636 Group stores and growing digital engagement (monthly active app users up 25% to 17.1 million in FY26).
currentContext.strategies: JFL is positioned as one of India's largest and most respected organised food-service platforms and the world's largest Domino's franchisee by store count, having evolved over three decades from a single Domino's store (1996) into a scaled, technology-led, multi-brand, multi-geography food-tech powerhouse.|The Company maintains a formal Dividend Distribution Policy (disclosed on its website) providing guidance for the declaration and pay-out of dividends. It also maintains a Policy on Materiality of and Dealing with Related Party Transactions, modified during FY26 (effective February 10, 2026) to align with amendments to the Listing Regulations, and a Code of Conduct for Prevention of Insider Trading governing dealing in the Company's securities by Designated Persons.
currentContext.expansion: The Group's store network expanded by a net 351 stores in FY26 to 3,636 restaurants across India, Turkey, Sri Lanka and Bangladesh (Azerbaijan/Georgia within the Turkey grouping), with India adding a net 289 stores. On the supply-chain side, the Company operationalised a new commissary/Food Park in Mumbai during FY26, intended to facilitate faster store-network expansion in western India, and moved processing of two additional ingredients (seasoning and sauce) in-house at its commissaries as part of its 'farm-to-fork' backward-integration model. On technology, the Company accelerated roll-out of Elate, an in-house-developed, Android-based, cloud-first POS and order-taking system built by a 250-member product/UX/tech/data-science team, integrating with the Company's direct-to-consumer platforms. The proprietary last-mile delivery rider network scaled beyond 45,000 partners, underpinning the Company's 20-minute delivery promise. Popeyes continued to expand, particularly into western India and southern markets (Bengaluru, Chennai), and is targeted to reach restaurant-level profitability by exit-FY27. Internationally, DP Eurasia (Turkey) repaid all local long-term debt during the year and began upstreaming dividends to service acquisition-related debt; the international store network stood at 1,074 stores at year-end. Management indicated capex intensity is expected to moderate structurally going forward as large supply-chain investments are largely behind, with free cash flow generation expected to strengthen steadily over the next three years.

Tier-2/Tier-3 city expansion, aided by improving infrastructure, is unlocking new growth pockets (industry-wide, ~94% of restaurant operators are targeting Tier II/III expansion with faster breakeven than metros).|Structural demand drivers cited: urbanisation of Tier II/III cities, a younger population (India median age 28.8, with over 65% of the population under 35), growth in nuclear households (increasing transaction frequency and per-capita out-of-home spend), 'value-led premiumization' (tiered menus balancing affordability and premium quality), a consumer shift toward trusted branded formats, and rising food-delivery/digital-ordering penetration.|The online food-delivery market is projected to expand from Rs.790 billion (FY25) to Rs.1.7-2.2 trillion by FY30 at a 17-23% CAGR, and still represents only ~11% of total food-services spend, indicating a long multi-year runway despite already contributing 60-70% of transactions for leading QSR players.

risks.note: Operations span sourcing, food preparation and service, where food safety hazards or contamination could impact consumer well-being, erode brand reputation/trust, trigger regulatory fines or sanctions, and cause temporary closures, product recalls or supply-chain disruption; financial implications include recall/disposal costs, alternative-supplier costs, penalties, and legal fees/settlements from affected consumers or regulators.

risks.risk: Employee and delivery-workforce health, safety and wellbeing
risks.note: Given the scale of the workforce engaged daily in food preparation, delivery logistics and diverse urban environments, unsafe conditions could raise attrition, harm morale/productivity, damage reputation via negative publicity, and generate medical/rehabilitation/claims costs, insurance premium increases, and fines/litigation for OHS non-compliance.

Maintaining ethical conduct across an increasingly interconnected and scrutinised business environment is flagged as a risk area; perceived ethical lapses could affect organisational culture, regulatory compliance and reputation, with financial implications from legal investigations/lawsuits, fines/penalties and lost sales from negative publicity.

risks.risk: ESG framework, environmental and regulatory compliance
risks.note: The evolving landscape of ESG frameworks/regulations and changing stakeholder (investor, regulator, community) expectations creates a risk of non-compliance with statutory requirements and negative publicity around sustainable-business practices, with financial implications including legal liabilities, fines/penalties and sales/profitability impact.

Increasing reliance on digital ordering, mobile and cloud touchpoints exposes the Company to hacking, ransomware and social-engineering threats that could cause unauthorised disclosure of Company/consumer/employee data, business disruption, financial losses and reputational damage; the Company notes its IT infrastructure aligns with ISO 27001 and the NIST Cyber Security Framework and reported no information security breaches in FY26.

one-line thesis: Jubilant FoodWorks gained pizza market share despite Q4 LFL growth deceleration to 0.2%, driven by conscious reduction in minimum order value to Rs.99 and premium product launches; near-term margin compression from 120 bps energy inflation and labor cost hikes is expected, but structural improvements in gross margin and capex efficiency support 200 bps margin expansion target over two years.
financial scorecard: Revenue: +6% YoY (LFL); EBITDA/margin: 20.1% (down 100 bps YoY due to energy/labor inflation); PAT (reported): -5% YoY; PAT (normalized): +2% YoY (ex-one-offs); order book: N/A; net debt: Rs. 1,200 Cr (down from Rs. 1,400 Cr YoY, driven by strong cash flow)
guidance: Revenue growth: 5-7% LFL annual; margin: 200 bps expansion over 2 years; order inflow: N/A; capex/commissioning: Rs. 1,800-2,000 Cr for 230-250 new stores (capex/store down 20% YoY for 3 years)
segment / subsidiary detail: Pizza: 85% of revenue; Delivery: 76% of sales (up from 72% YoY); Dine-in: low base, decelerated growth; Premium products (Big Big Pizza, Sourdough): 15% of sales, 300 bps higher margin; Dunkin': losses narrowing; Popeyes/Hong's: dilutive but under control
growth verticals / optionality: Expansion into Tier 3/4 cities with smaller 600-700 sq ft delivery-focused stores; potential for Dunkin' profitability by FY28; untapped premium product penetration; delivery fleet electrification scale-up
margins & cost dynamics: Gross margin: 75.5% (up 100 bps YoY) driven by waste reduction, premium mix, calibrated pricing; EBITDA margin: pressured by 120 bps energy cost inflation (LPG/PNG), 50-60 bps labor inflation (minimum wage hikes + delivery mix), and 20-30 bps commodity inflation; net margin compression expected in FY27Q1-Q2
capex / expansion: Rs. 1,800-2,000 Cr for FY27; 230-250 new stores; capex/store down 20% YoY for 3 consecutive years due to smaller store formats (600-700 sq ft); 40% of new stores are delivery-only; conversion of LPG to electric/PNG ovens underway
capital allocation: Prioritizing growth capex (store expansion); debt reduction (net debt down Rs. 200 Cr YoY); reinvestment in premium product R&D and delivery fleet electrification; no dividend increase planned in FY27
risks & watch-items: Sustained LPG price volatility; wage inflation across 11+ states; delivery mix increasing labor cost burden; competitive discounting from Domino's; consumer sensitivity to price hikes; supply chain disruption from geopolitical events
management quality / tone: Confident on long-term growth (5-7% LFL) and margin recovery (200 bps over 2 years); transparent on near-term headwinds; focused on volume over short-term margin; proactive on cost control, electrification, and premiumization; dismissive of short-term noise
non-obvious takeaways: Electric delivery fleet now covers majority of operations, reducing LPG exposure; internal R&D kits for oven conversion have cut capex and improved operational resilience; premium product mix (Sourdough, Big Big Pizza) is driving margin expansion despite lower average ticket size

hero.oneLiner: Jubilant FoodWorks Limited is one of India's largest organised food-service platforms and the world's largest Domino's franchisee by store count, operating a multi-brand, multi-country QSR platform across six emerging markets.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Jubilant FoodWorks Limited is one of India's largest organised food-service platforms and the world's largest Domino's franchisee by store count, operating a multi-brand, multi-country QSR platform across six emerging markets.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Jubilant FoodWorks Limited (JFL), incorporated in 1995, is an emerging-markets food-service company whose Group network comprises 3,636 stores across India, Turkey, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Azerbaijan and Georgia. It holds franchise rights for three global brands - Domino's, Popeyes and Dunkin' - and operates two own-brands, Hong's Kitchen (an Indo-Chinese QSR brand in India) and COFFY (a cafe brand in Turkey). The Company serves over 50 million customers annually across more than 650 cities through an integrated ecosystem of stores, supply chain infrastructure, technology platforms and last-mile delivery operations.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- India remained among the fastest-growing major economies in FY26 (real GDP growth estimated ~6.5%-6.8% per the Economic Survey FY26), supported by resilient domestic demand, strong public capex, healthy banking liquidity and continued formalisation — reinforcing India's position as a structural growth engine.
- Government fiscal measures (tax rationalisation, targeted relief for middle-income households) are expected to gradually improve consumer sentiment and discretionary spending over the medium term.
- Improving macro stability, supportive fiscal policy, infrastructure investment and easing inflation are expected to support a gradual recovery in discretionary spending, creating a favourable medium-to-long-term backdrop for organised food services, branded consumption and convenience-led digital platforms.
- The organised QSR segment continues to gain share from the large unorganised food-services sector as consumers shift toward branded, trusted, technology-enabled platforms; organised food services (QSR/cloud kitchens/cafes) share rose to ~45-50% of the overall market in FY26 (from 35-40% in 2019) and is projected to reach ~55% by 2030.
- The Delivery channel remains a structurally important growth engine, accounting for a dominant (often 60-70%) share of transactions for leading brands, while dine-in and takeaway saw some moderation amid affordability pressures and evolving post-pandemic consumer behaviour.
- India remains significantly underpenetrated in organised QSR versus global benchmarks (lower store density per million population than the US or China), presenting a large multi-decadal opportunity; Tier-2/Tier-3 city expansion, aided by improving infrastructure, is unlocking new growth pockets (industry-wide, ~94% of restaurant operators are targeting Tier II/III expansion with faster breakeven than metros).
- Structural demand drivers cited: urbanisation of Tier II/III cities, a younger population (India median age 28.8, with over 65% of the population under 35), growth in nuclear households (increasing transaction frequency and per-capita out-of-home spend), 'value-led premiumization' (tiered menus balancing affordability and premium quality), a consumer shift toward trusted branded formats, and rising food-delivery/digital-ordering penetration.
- The online food-delivery market is projected to expand from Rs.790 billion (FY25) to Rs.1.7-2.2 trillion by FY30 at a 17-23% CAGR, and still represents only ~11% of total food-services spend, indicating a long multi-year runway despite already contributing 60-70% of transactions for leading QSR players.

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Gross margin: 75.5% (up 100 bps YoY) driven by waste reduction, premium mix, calibrated pricing; EBITDA margin: pressured by 120 bps energy cost inflation (LPG/PNG), 50-60 bps labor inflation (minimum wage hikes + delivery mix), and 20-30 bps commodity inflation; net margin compression expected in FY27Q1-Q2

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Prioritizing growth capex (store expansion); debt reduction (net debt down Rs. 200 Cr YoY); reinvestment in premium product R&D and delivery fleet electrification; no dividend increase planned in FY27

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The Group's store network expanded by a net 351 stores in FY26 to 3,636 restaurants across India, Turkey, Sri Lanka and Bangladesh (Azerbaijan/Georgia within the Turkey grouping), with India adding a net 289 stores. On the supply-chain side, the Company operationalised a new commissary/Food Park in Mumbai during FY26, intended to facilitate faster store-network expansion in western India, and moved processing of two additional ingredients (seasoning and sauce) in-house at its commissaries as part of its 'farm-to-fork' backward-integration model. On technology, the Company accelerated roll-out of Elate, an in-house-developed, Android-based, cloud-first POS and order-taking system built by a 250-member product/UX/tech/data-science team, integrating with the Company's direct-to-consumer platforms. The proprietary last-mile delivery rider network scaled beyond 45,000 partners, underpinning the Company's 20-minute delivery promise. Popeyes continued to expand, particularly into western India and southern markets (Bengaluru, Chennai), and is targeted to reach restaurant-level profitability by exit-FY27. Internationally, DP Eurasia (Turkey) repaid all local long-term debt during the year and began upstreaming dividends to service acquisition-related debt; the international store network stood at 1,074 stores at year-end. Management indicated capex intensity is expected to moderate structurally going forward as large supply-chain investments are largely behind, with free cash flow generation expected to strengthen steadily over the next three years.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident on long-term growth (5-7% LFL) and margin recovery (200 bps over 2 years); transparent on near-term headwinds; focused on volume over short-term margin; proactive on cost control, electrification, and premiumization; dismissive of short-term noise

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Brand Leadership and Innovation: Domino's Pizza is described as one of India's most iconic and dominant food-service brands with significant market share in the organised pizza category, built over three decades of local menu innovation, value positioning and fast delivery.
- Multi-brand portfolio spanning pizza (Domino's), fried chicken (Popeyes) and Indo-Chinese (Hong's Kitchen) targeting diverse consumer occasions and price points, capturing a larger share of wallet.
- Scaled Digital Ecosystem: proprietary AI platforms - Location.AI (site selection/catchment optimisation), Restaurant.AI (computer-vision store monitoring, dynamic delivery-zone/discount management) and Delivery.AI (rider onboarding under 30 minutes, order allocation) - are described as strengthening the Company's competitive moat.
- Common operating platform (supply chain, technology, store operations, analytics, talent) that allows JFL to scale multiple brands and geographies more efficiently and improve capital efficiency.
- Scale as the world's largest Domino's franchisee by store count, with 3,636 Group stores and growing digital engagement (monthly active app users up 25% to 17.1 million in FY26).

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Sustained LPG price volatility; wage inflation across 11+ states; delivery mix increasing labor cost burden; competitive discounting from Domino's; consumer sensitivity to price hikes; supply chain disruption from geopolitical events

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Electric delivery fleet now covers majority of operations, reducing LPG exposure; internal R&D kits for oven conversion have cut capex and improved operational resilience; premium product mix (Sourdough, Big Big Pizza) is driving margin expansion despite lower average ticket size

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
